title: Entropy and mutual information of measures

ProbabilityTheory.measureEntropy.statement: For a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $S$, the entropy $H_m[\mu]$ is the (Shannon) entropy of the normalized measure $(\mu(S))^{-1}\mu$; normalizing by $(\mu(S))^{-1}$ extends the definition from probability measures to finite measures.

ProbabilityTheory.measureEntropy_of_isPr.statement: For a probability measure $\mu$ on $S$, $H_m[\mu] = \sum_{s\in S} \mathrm{negMulLog}(\mu(\{s\}))$ (a possibly infinite sum, $\mathrm{tsum}$), where $\mathrm{negMulLog}(x) = -x\log x$.
ProbabilityTheory.measureEntropy_of_isPr.sketch: Direct from the definition of $H_m$, since the normalizing factor is $1$ for a probability measure.

ProbabilityTheory.FiniteSupport.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $S$ has finite support if there exists a finite set $A\subseteq S$ whose complement has measure zero, $\mu(A^c)=0$.

ProbabilityTheory.integrable_of_finiteSu.statement: If $\mu$ is a measure on $S$ with finite support (under the standing assumptions, including countability of $S$), then every function $f$ on $S$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
ProbabilityTheory.integrable_of_finiteSu.sketch: The finite support of $\mu$ is a finite set whose complement is $\mu$-null, so the integral reduces to a finite sum of values of $f$ weighted by the (finite) masses of points.

ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo.statement: For a measure $\mu$ on a product $S\times T$, the mutual information $I_m[\mu]$ between its two marginals, namely $I_m[\mu] = H_m[\pi_1{}_*\mu] + H_m[\pi_2{}_*\mu] - H_m[\mu]$ with $\pi_1,\pi_2$ the coordinate projections.

ProbabilityTheory.measureEntropy_of_isPr.statement: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $S$ and $A\subseteq S$ a finite set with $\mu(A^c)=0$. Then $H_m[\mu] = \sum_{s\in A}\mathrm{negMulLog}(\mu(\{s\}))$, where $\mathrm{negMulLog}(x)=-x\log x$.
ProbabilityTheory.measureEntropy_of_isPr.sketch: This follows from the expression of $H_m[\mu]$ as a sum over a finite set carrying all the mass.

ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_nonn.statement: For a (finitely supported, under the standing assumptions) measure $\mu$ on $S\times U$: $0 \le I_m[\mu]$, and moreover $I_m[\mu]=0$ if and only if for every $p=(p_1,p_2)\in S\times U$, $\mu(\{p\}) = (\pi_1{}_*\mu)(\{p_1\})\cdot(\pi_2{}_*\mu)(\{p_2\})$, i.e. $\mu$ is the product of its marginals.
ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_nonn.sketch: Write each of the three entropies in $I_m[\mu]$ as a finite sum of $\mathrm{negMulLog}$ over the (finite) support using measureEntropy_of_isProbabilityMeasure_finite, handling the zero measure separately; the resulting sum is a relative-entropy-type expression whose nonnegativity and equality case give the claim.

ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_of_n.statement: If $\mu$ is not a finite measure, then $I_m[\mu]=0$.
ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_of_n.sketch: Unfold $I_m$ in terms of $H_m$; each entropy term vanishes for a non-finite measure (and its marginals are then not finite either).

ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_univ.statement: For every measure $\mu$ on $S\times U$, $I_m[(\mu(S\times U))^{-1}\,\mu] = I_m[\mu]$.
ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_univ.sketch: Split into cases: if $\mu$ is not finite, both sides vanish by measureMutualInfo_of_not_isFiniteMeasure (and the zero-measure case is trivial); otherwise unfold $I_m$ into $H_m$ terms and use that $H_m$ is invariant under scaling by $(\mu(\text{univ}))^{-1}$.

ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_nonn.statement: For a measure $\mu$ on $S\times U$ (under the standing finite-support assumptions), $0\le I_m[\mu]$.
ProbabilityTheory.measureMutualInfo_nonn.sketch: If $\mu$ is not finite, $I_m[\mu]=0$; otherwise replace $\mu$ by its normalization using measureMutualInfo_univ_smul (which still has finite support) and apply the first part of measureMutualInfo_nonneg_aux.
